simple.meaning: שִׁמֻּר (shimmur) is a Hebrew word meaning “an observance.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שִׁמֻּר (H8107) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 12:42, with occurrences in Exodus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שִׁמֻּר (H8107) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שִׁמֻּר (H8107) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שִׁמֻּר (shimmur) / H8107 is traced through Exodus 12:42 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H8107. shimmur [ שִׁמֻּר ] noun [masculine] watching, vigil (so Di; > observance ); — plural לי שִׁמֻּרִים ׳לֵיל Exod 12:42 a night of vigils to ׳שׁ יִשׁ ׳לְכָלבְּֿנֵי ׳י, 12:42 .

occurrences.englishText: It is a night to be much observed to Yahweh for bringing them out from the land of Egypt. This is that night of Yahweh, to be much observed by all the children of Israel throughout their generations.
